It looks like 'Waccamaw', it has the color of 'Waccamaw'… but it's not 'Waccamaw' which is almost unobtainable in France.
So, I console myself with my flava var.atropurpurea F130H MSrba which has the same colors when opened.
Obviously, everything turns purple afterwards, but for a few days the illusion remains....

It doesn't have its color this year due to a number of factors...but I was told by Jeremiah Harris that the plant I received as "FCPE #1" is almost certainly this cultivar, and the behavior I've seen so far matches. Brick red exterior, starts bright yellow inside, rather dwarf pitcher habits, and even when not full color as seen by this picture even the lids definitely start out matching the tubes
S. 'Waccamaw' by Hawken Carlton, on Flickr

Saw Mike's update and snapped a quick pic this morning to share. Still one of my all-time favorite plants. This is my sixth year with it and it's always a major centerpiece of the collection. The bright red is quite unique and really jumps out even next to other red tube flavas. A plant with such amazing color that's so easy to grow is pretty hard to come by!

Here's my mother plant alongside 'Adrian Slack':

posts.body_html: First season for my piece to grow outdoors. Before that I trimmed off all phyllodia to eliminate pre-existing powedery mildew. This move is about 90% stupid and 100% costly, with the help of four April frosts. The spring flush decided to say “MEH” . Hey, let’s look on the bright side— a stunning cuprea!
